defects: Drops the semiring structure entirely: gold has C : Set (Set α) (a semiring of sets) with a content m : AddContent E C defined only on C; produced instead makes C : Set α → E a function defined on ALL subsets of α, eliminating the core 'partial domain that is a semiring' structure the theorem is about.
Missing hypothesis IsSetSemiring C (or any semiring-type restriction) — essential to the informal statement ('semiring of measurable sets').

hC_add imposes finite additivity for every pair of disjoint sets in the whole power set, not the semiring-specific additive-content axioms (AddContent, which also requires e.g. content of ∅ = 0 and uses semiring set-difference decompositions) — a different algebraic condition than gold's hm on AddContent.
Missing measurability hypothesis h'C : ∀ s ∈ C, MeasurableSet s (not even expressible in the produced formulation since C's 'domain' isn't a sub-collection).

E is only required to be SeminormedAddCommGroup with no CompleteSpace assumption, whereas gold requires NormedAddCommGroup and CompleteSpace E — completeness is dropped, weakening/altering a hypothesis needed for vector-measure extension results.

Type/units mismatch: hC_dom and the conclusion compare ‖C s‖ (real-valued norm from SeminormedAddCommGroup) to μ s (ℝ≥0∞-valued), whereas gold consistently uses the extended norm ‖·‖ₑ : ℝ≥0∞; this does not match gold's ENNReal-based domination and likely doesn't typecheck as written.

Conclusion ∀ s, C s = ν s demands equality on ALL sets (not just s ∈ C as in gold), which combined with VectorMeasure's convention of vanishing on non-measurable sets forces C to vanish off the measurable sets — an unstated, unintended extra constraint not present in gold, and overall changes the theorem into a different, non-equivalent claim (C would already have to be essentially countably additive everywhere, not merely finitely additive on a semiring's worth of sets).
